source_locus: Kelly et al. 2014, Abstract (PNAS 111:5012-5017; fMRI attribution task, TPJ; single-pulse TMS to TPJ sites); Graziano & Webb 2015 p. 4 (hemispatial neglect as loss of subjective awareness, no substrate named)
quote_1: When the TMS was targeted to the same cortical sites that had become active during the social attribution task, the subjects showed symptoms of visual neglect in that their detection of visual stimuli was significantly affected.
quote_2: Activity associated with this task was found bilaterally within the temporoparietal junction (TPJ) among other areas.

quote_1: The most parsimonious assumption is that the principles involved in the production of “pain images” are the same as those involved in the production of other sensory images such as visual images, auditory images, etc.

note: Code and polarity agree; claim_text revised so that it rests on the 2013 article alone: the 2013 text treats pain (with somatosensory, affective and homeostatic components) as conscious sensory content produced by the same mechanism as exteroceptive images, and lists the insula for its interoceptive aspects (p. 10). The 'affective consciousness' / tripartite exteroceptive-interoceptive-affective wording of the current claim is in the 2016 book, which remains unreachable (MIT Press, closed; doi resolve 403) - that part of the claim is secondary. Qualification on p. 17: some low-level visceral-sensory paths (airway chemoreceptors, carotid baroreceptors) 'are not consciously perceived at all'; interoceptive content is conscious only where it enters an isomorphic hierarchy.

source_locus: Park et al. 2014, Abstract (Nat. Neurosci. 17:612-618); Tallon-Baudry et al. 2018, Abstract (Cortex 102:139-149); Park & Tallon-Baudry 2014, Abstract (Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 369:20130208)
quote_1: neural events locked to heartbeats before stimulus onset predict the detection of a faint visual grating in the posterior right inferior parietal lobule and the ventral anterior cingulate cortex
quote_2: The impact of spontaneous fluctuations of neural responses to heartbeats on visual detection is as large as the impact of explicit manipulations of spatial attention in perceptual tasks.
sections_searched: Abstracts only (PubMed/PMC records). Full texts not reachable: Nature Neuroscience closed; Cortex hybrid OA copy behind publisher bot check, EPFL Infoscience repository copy behind WAF; Phil Trans B PMC record has no XML body and PDF is behind a proof-of-work challenge.
note: The abstract sentences themselves name the modulator (heartbeat-locked neural response amplitude before stimulus onset) and the effect (visual detection), so EXPLICIT positive modulation is grounded even without full text; confidence 3 retained. Park et al. 2014 is an empirical report; the theoretical statement is in Tallon-Baudry et al. 2018 ('the neural monitoring of the heart, affects visual perception').
